description: Unify runner capacity to a single source of truth (RunnerStatusService) so sidebar, Dashboard pulse, runner status page, and CLI report identical used/max slot values; decouple capacity from AgentSession visibility counts.

tasks.title: Unify /agent/status sidebar capacity to RunnerStatusService source
tasks.description: Add an aggregate capacity accessor on RunnerStatusService (e.g. GetCapacityAsync(projectId) summing UsedSlots/TotalSlots over online/available runner views, matching ListAvailableRunnersAsync 'online' semantics) and rewire the GET /agent/status route to source both the top-level Capacity and each Runners[].Active/Max from RunnerStatusService.GetRunnersAsync views instead of grouping activeAgents by runner. Drop LoadPersistedSlotsByRunnerAsync and activeSlotsByRunner; change AgentStatusResponse.Create to take runner-status views (Active=UsedSlots, Max=TotalSlots) instead of persistedSlotsByRunner. activeAgents remains the source for the ActiveAgents[] visibility list and the Running flag only. Rewrite ApiContractSpecs and RuntimeEntrySpecs (including the direct Create call at RuntimeEntrySpecs.cs:195) so they no longer assert capacity == active AgentSession count, and add a divergence spec proving runner active works > visible active AgentSessions yields capacity.active reflecting runner works.
acceptanceCriteria: RunnerStatusService exposes a single aggregate accessor returning summed (UsedSlots, TotalSlots) over online runners, with no second capacity service or duplicate DTO introduced.

GET /agent/status.capacity.active/max and each Runners[].Active/Max derive from RunnerStatusService runner-status views (runtime active workflow works distinct by owner id + persisted slots), not from activeAgents grouped by runner.

AgentStatusResponse.Create no longer accepts persistedSlotsByRunner and no longer computes activeSlotsByRunner from activeAgents; the direct constructor caller in RuntimeEntrySpecs.cs:195 is updated and compiles.
activeAgents still populates the ActiveAgents[] visibility list and the Running flag, but is never read for any slot count.
ApiContractSpecs / RuntimeEntrySpecs assertions that tied capacity to active AgentSession count are removed or rewritten to the unified source.

New divergence spec: when a runner grain holds more active workflow works than there are visible active AgentSessions, /agent/status.capacity.active equals the runner active-works count and is not clamped to the AgentSession count.
RunnerStatusProjectionSpecs (GetRunnersAsync_CapacityUsesPersistedSlots etc.) still pass, pinning the authoritative source.
`npm test` (server, dotnet test with TreatWarningsAsErrors) passes.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Runner/Services/RunnerStatusService.cs (aggregate accessor), packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Api/AgentRoutes.cs (/agent/status route + AgentStatusResponse.Create), updated server specs
tasks.notes: This task owns the D2 aggregate accessor since it has no standalone value without a consumer; T-002 reuses it. Keep the online/available runner filter identical to the current ListAvailableRunnersAsync semantics so /agent/status and /runners agree on which runners count toward max.

tasks.title: Unify /agent/activity Dashboard pulse slots to RunnerStatusService source
tasks.description: Rewire the GET /agent/activity route to call RunnerStatusService.GetCapacityAsync(project.Id) and pass the resulting (used, max) into AgentSessionQuerier.GetActivityAsync so summary.slots reflects the unified runner-capacity source. Drop the runnerIds parameter from GetActivityAsync (it fed only the runnerCount+1 heuristic) and remove the local cards.Count(active) / runnerCount+1 computation in ActivitySlotUsageDto; the querier performs no capacity math of its own and stays session-pure (do not inject RunnerStatusService into it). Rewrite AgentSessionSpecs assertions that pinned slots to active-session-card count or runnerCount+1, and add a divergence assertion that pulse active slots reflect runner works when sessions diverge.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /agent/activity.summary.slots.active/max are sourced from RunnerStatusService.GetCapacityAsync (runner active workflow works + persisted slots), identical to /runners[].capacity for the same online runner set at the same time.

AgentSessionQuerier.GetActivityAsync no longer accepts runnerIds and no longer computes ActivitySlotUsageDto from cards.Count(active) or runnerCount+1; it uses the capacity values supplied by the route.
AgentSessionQuerier remains session-pure: RunnerStatusService is not injected into it; the route is the orchestrator that supplies capacity.
AgentSessionSpecs assertions tying summary.slots to active-session-card count or runnerCount+1 are removed or rewritten to the unified source.
Divergence assertion: when runner active works exceed visible active AgentSessions, summary.slots.active reflects the runner active-works count.
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 for the RunnerStatusService.GetCapacityAsync aggregate accessor. Wire shape { active, max } of ActivitySlotUsageDto is preserved; only value derivation changes (D3/D4).

tasks.title: Fix IssueDetailPage client-side capacity gating to use server capacity
tasks.description: Change IssueDetailPage.tsx isCapacityFull (currently activeAgents.length >= maxConcurrent at line ~410) to gate on the server-provided capacity values (capacity.active >= capacity.max), removing the last client-side spot that treats activeAgents as a capacity source. activeAgents continues to drive visibility (isAgentRunningOnThis, the 'N agents running on other issues' indicator) but not capacity gating. Update web unit tests covering the capacity-full gating behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: IssueDetailPage.tsx computes isCapacityFull from the server capacity.active/capacity.max (matching derive-runtime-decision.ts canonical gating), not from activeAgents.length.
activeAgents is still used for AgentSession visibility (isAgentRunningOnThis, other-issues running indicator) and is not removed.
Web unit tests for IssueDetailPage capacity-full gating are updated to assert the new derivation and pass.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.notes: Behaviorally depends on T-001 so the server supplies correct capacity.active values; code change is independent and web unit tests mock the server response. derive-runtime-decision.ts already gates correctly and needs no change (D5).
